query: Which method can be used for oxidation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Adding Al, Cr, and Si elements to refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) can form a dense oxidation film, improving high-temperature oxidation resistance.
generation.intervention: Adding Al, Cr, and Si elements
generation.mechanism: Formation of a protective oxide scale
generation.baseline: RHEAs without Al, Cr, and Si elements
generation.boundary: High-temperature oxidation resistance of RHEAs with and without Al, Cr, and Si elements
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Al, Cr, and Si elements required to achieve optimal oxidation resistance is uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of RHEAs with and without Al, Cr, and Si elements under high-temperature oxidation conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the RHEAs without Al, Cr, and Si elements exhibit similar or better high-temperature oxidation resistance than those with these elements, the hypothesis is falsified.
